text: This is the Aegis-12 Fiduciary Dashboard — a real-time control plane for autonomous AI agents.
On the left, fiduciary policy rules enforce hard limits on what agents can do with your money.
Let's trigger a live intent stream. This sends a micro-transaction to real hardware running inside a Phala TDX enclave.
The request is now routing through our Fiduciary Firewall to the live Intel hardware. This is real attestation, not a simulation.
DCAP verified. The hardware has cryptographically proven its integrity. The transaction is signed and submitted to Solana Devnet.
Here in the Verifier Registry, you can see the real transaction hash, the round trip latency, and a clickable proof link to Solana Explorer.
This is the actual on-chain transaction with our aegis oracle memo.
Now let's demonstrate the circuit breaker. This simulates a malicious agent attempting an unauthorized drain.
Lockdown initiated. The enclave is sealed. The private key physically cannot sign any more transactions.
Now we recover with a multisig override and trigger another live transaction to prove resilience.
Every action, approved or blocked, is cryptographically anchored to Solana. This is the mathematical cage.
